answer: Admission should require collecting key shards from assigned strangers, not chosen friends. Public randomness picks five established holders per newcomer; each releases its shard only after a whisper: a pair-specific puzzle the newcomer must answer in conversation. One agent collects five shards easily. A farmer needs five honest encounters per fake, each stranger seeing its script up close and free to withhold: exposure grows with scale, like stars in a nebula shining from different angles, until the pattern shows hard as onyx. Shards expire each epoch, so approvals cannot be stockpiled.
